messages:
Maya S: Heads up — saw a latency tail spike for small-chat workload when routing fell back to the variant with older kernels. Repro on canary, looks like batching gets fragmented and KV miss amplifies the cost.

Kevin L: Oof. Numbers?

Maya S: P90 for the fallback path jumped from ~72ms -> ~180ms. Batcher hist shows a lot of tiny batches (1-2 reqs). Token budget is 64; compat set mismatch seems to cause fragmentation across the queue.

Raj P: Did the kernel selector change last week? I recall a tweak to prefer fused-attn on short seqs.

Maya S: Yup. Selector picks `kernel=v3` for main variant but `v2` for fallback (no fused kv prefetch). Quick debug dump: 

```
[selector] model=redwood-small variant=main -> kernel=v3 fused_attn
[selector] model=redwood-small variant=fallback -> kernel=v2 matmul
[batcher] batch_size_hist={1:62%, 2:25%, 3+:13%}
[queue] avg_wait_ms=6 token_budget=64 slice_target=32
```

Olivia C: So two problems: kernel capability mismatch (per-token time diff) + batching fragmentation because compat grouping is too coarse. We should either align kernel capabilities across variants or make the queueer group by compat fingerprint.

Alice M: Agreed on compat fingerprint grouping. Fast hash over (model, quant, kernel_caps, seq_bucket) should let the coalescer favor homogeneous batches. That will reduce variance.

Maya S: I tried a quick change: prefer same-kernel coalescing with a +3ms extra wait cap for matching-fingerprint. Short smoke: p90_fallback dropped to ~95ms; global p90 moved +6ms. Logs: 

```
before: p90_all=86ms p90_fallback=180ms
after:  p90_all=92ms p90_fallback=95ms
tradeoff: +6ms main path
```

Kevin L: Nice. Any throughput regressions for large batches? We need to be careful not to hurt heavy throughput workloads.

Maya S: We gated it: if batch_size >= 16, policy switches to throughput-first. In perf runs we didn't see throughput drops.

Raj P: Also worth noting KV cache warmup: fallback variant misses prefix cache much more often, so each request does more per-token work. We should track kv_hit_rate per-compat.

Maya S: Added kv_hit_rate metric: kv_hit_rate{compat=main} ~= 0.78 vs kv_hit_rate{compat=fallback} ~= 0.12. That gap explains extra GPU ops and latency.

Olivia C: Low KV hit is a big factor. Options: route fallback to warmed replicas, do on-demand KV prefetch for hot prefixes, or align model variants so prefixes share cache keys.

Alice M: CPU fallback isn't great — per-token slower. Better to warm the KV or prefetch hot prefixes per-customer. We could also add a small pre-warm probe for new compat groups.

Maya S: Proposed next steps:
1) Align kernel capability flags across variants where feasible (Olivia).
2) Implement compat-fingerprint grouping in the queue policy (I will own). Try a +3ms wait cap as a starting point.
3) Emit kv_hit_rate per-compat and alert when drop >30% vs baseline (Raj).
4) Perf canary and throughput regression tests.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for eng-runtime patch/variant-queue-grouping @canary

Kevin L: Who owns items 2 and 3?

Maya S: I'll own 2, Raj will own 3, Olivia to validate kernel alignment.

Olivia C: I'll attempt to push kernel flag parity for the fallback tonight; if not possible we should consider reverting last week's selector change.

Raj P: I'll add the kv_hit_rate metric and compat label schema (model|variant|quant|kernelcap|seqbucket). Need a quick schema PR.

Maya S: Great. Keep updates here. If anyone hits new p99 regressions, ping me directly.

:thumbsup:
